candidate_windows.window_text: In accordance with prior work (Bao et al., 2019), we use pre-trained fastText (Joulin et al., 2016) for word embedding. As a feature extractor, we employ a BiLSTM with 128 hidden units and set the number of hidden units for the reference layers to 256. We take cosine similarity as the distance function. The model is implemented in PyTorch (Paszke et al., 2017) using the Adam (Kingma and Ba, 2014) optimizer with a $10^{-4}$ learning rate. For the sake of a fair comparison, we follow the identical evaluation protocol and train/val/test split as Bao et al. (2019). The model parameters and reference layers are randomly initialized. During meta-training, we perform 100 training episodes per epoch. Meanwhile, we apply early stopping if the accuracy on the validation set does not increase after 20 epochs. We evaluate the model performance based on a total of one thousand testing episodes and present the average accuracy across five different random seeds. All experiments are conducted with NVIDIA V100 GPUs.
